newsitem.title: UK: Barclays chief to head UK tax taskforce.
newsitem.headline: Barclays chief to head UK tax taskforce.

text.p: Martin Taylor, chief executive of Barclays Plc, will spearhead a government drive to modernise Britain's tax and benefit system, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced on Monday.

Taylor will lead a Whitehall taskforce on tax and benefits aimed at delivering the new government's pledge to streamline and modernise the system and to promote incentives to work, a Treasury statement said.
He will spend about two days a month on average on the project, which is expected to last for about a year. He told Reuters his role would not affect his position at Barclays.

"There is bound to be a lot of reading involved but I have no intention of it interfering with my role at Barclays," he said, adding that his appointment had been discussed over the previous few weeks.

The taskforce will bring together civil servants from the Treasury, the Inland Revenue and the departments of Social Security and Education and Employment. It will work closely with ministers in those departments.
Brown said Taylor, who was appointed as Barclays' chief in 1993, would "bring to it a first rate mind and ability to find practical solutions to make a long-term difference."
"Today's appointment harnesses the drive of the private sector to the expertise of government departments to streamline both our tax and benefit systems," Brown said.
The theoretical scope for the taskforce was broadly laid out in Labour's election manifesto, Taylor said.
"The precise scope of the work will be sorted out by the committee which has yet to be set up. I've got some ideas but...it would be wrong for me to comment at this stage."

Social Security Secretary Harriet Harman said the taskforce would explore ways for the tax and benefits system to encourage people to move into work. "We want to tear down the barriers that keep people out of jobs and trapped on benefit," she said. "Work is the best form of welfare for people of working age."
Brown is due to hold a budget within weeks. He has pledged to levy a windfall tax on Britain's privatised utilities, using the proceeds to get 250,000 people into work.
